source: SPM Essay (older format, no trial paper named) · Essay on examinations
paragraphs: Examinations are a crucial part of the education system in Malaysia. From primary school to university, students are required to sit for various exams that assess their academic knowledge and skills. These exams play a significant role in determining a student’s progress, grades, and future opportunities. However, there is ongoing debate about whether examinations are the best method to evaluate students.

In my opinion, examinations are useful, but they are not always a fair representation of a student's abilities. Exams put a lot of pressure on students to perform well within a limited time frame, which can lead to stress and anxiety. Some students may excel in exam settings, while others, who may have a deeper understanding of the subject, might not do as well due to nerves or time constraints.

There are both advantages and disadvantages to having examinations. One of the main advantages is that exams provide a standardized way to measure a student’s knowledge and compare their performance with their peers. They also motivate students to study and prepare thoroughly. On the other hand, exams focus heavily on memorization rather than understanding, which can limit critical thinking and creativity. Additionally, the stress of exams may negatively affect students' mental health.

As for whether examinations should be abolished, I believe they should not be entirely removed but reformed. While exams serve a purpose in education, alternative assessment methods such as project-based learning or continuous assessment could be incorporated to provide a more balanced evaluation of students’ skills and knowledge.

In conclusion, examinations in Malaysia play an important role in education, but they also come with challenges. By improving the examination system and combining it with other forms of assessment, we can ensure a fairer and more holistic approach to evaluating students.
